name: Danish
script: Latin with extra letters: æ, ø, å; left to right
basis: University beginner Danish (UBC DANI 100, textbook Puls 1), first term
src: University of British Columbia: DANI 100 syllabus (2022W T1), weekly schedule with grammar and pronunciation, textbook Puls 1
Danes Worldwide (danes.dk): content of Danish for Beginners A1, themes and communication goals for three terms
elon.io: Danish grammar A1 learner path (a grammar website's path, not a course syllabus)
note: The early order follows UBC DANI 100 (alphabet and introductions, vowels, negation and adverbs, nationalities, question words and pronouns, numbers, nouns, time, present tense, inversion, weekdays, family and plurals, past tense). The UBC course reaches the past only at the end of term; danes.dk supplied later A1 topics (café, prices, home, likes). Modal verbs, possessives, adjectives, directions and all titles are common course practice and my own judgment.
hardest: Pronunciation far from spelling: soft d, swallowed endings, many vowel sounds
The stød (glottal catch) that can change a word's meaning
Numbers 50-90: halvtreds, tres, halvfjerds, firs, halvfems
en or et for each noun, and the definite ending (bilen, huset)

items: Vowels: many sounds for few letters
Soft d, silent letters and the stød
Introducing yourself: Jeg hedder…, Jeg kommer fra…
Pronouns: jeg, du, han, hun, vi, I, de, and mig, dig
Present tense in -r: jeg bor, hun taler
ikke: negation and adverbs in the sentence
Nationalities and languages: Jeg er amerikaner, Jeg taler engelsk
Questions: hvad, hvor, hvem, hvornår, hvordan, and yes/no questions
Numbers and prices: halvtreds, tres, halvfjerds, kroner
en and et: the two genders
Telling the time: halv tre, kvart over
Verb in second place: I dag arbejder jeg
Days and routines: om morgenen, om aftenen
Modal verbs + infinitive: vil, kan, skal, må
At the café: Jeg vil gerne have…, Hvad koster det?
Family and plural definite: børnene, forældrene
Adjectives: en stor bil, et stort hus, store huse
Likes: Jeg kan godt lide…, Jeg elsker…
Directions: til højre, til venstre, ligeud
Past tense: jeg arbejdede, jeg var, jeg havde
